questions.stem: Who was the first Governor-General of Bengal under the Regulating Act, 1773?
questions.explanation: Warren Hastings (1773-85) was the FIRST Governor-General of Bengal (Fort William) under the Regulating Act 1773 — which subordinated Bombay & Madras Presidencies to Bengal. Robert Clive was Governor of Bengal 1757-60 and 1765-67 (pre-dating the GG office). Key Hastings actions: founded Asiatic Society of Bengal (1784, by William Jones during his tenure), commissioned Charles Wilkins's Gita translation, First Anglo-Maratha War, Pitt's India Act 1784 passed during his tenure. Impeached 1787 in UK (acquitted 1795). Lord Cornwallis (1786-93) succeeded him — introduced Permanent Settlement 1793.

questions.stem: Who was the first Governor-General of India (of all British territories) under the Charter Act, 1833?
questions.explanation: Lord William Bentinck (GG of Bengal 1828-33; then GG of INDIA 1833-35) became the FIRST Governor-General of India (not just Bengal) under the Charter Act 1833 — which centralised legislative power and created the title. Key Bentinck reforms: abolition of SATI (1829, Regulation XVII via Raja Ram Mohan Roy's advocacy), suppression of THUGGEE (with William Sleeman), abolition of female infanticide, English as medium of higher education (Macaulay's Minute 1835 under his tenure). Lord Dalhousie (1848-56) — Doctrine of Lapse, annexed Awadh, railway 1853, postal 1854. Lord Canning (1856-58 GG, 1858-62 VICEROY) — straddled the transition when 1857 Revolt ended Company rule.

questions.stem: Who was the first VICEROY of India, after the Crown took direct control in 1858?
questions.explanation: LORD CANNING (1856-62) was both: (a) the LAST Governor-General of India under the Company (1856-58), and (b) the FIRST VICEROY of India when the Queen's Proclamation of 1 November 1858 (Government of India Act 1858) transferred power from the East India Company to the British Crown. Known as 'Clemency Canning' for his comparatively restrained handling of post-1857 reprisals. Ended Doctrine of Lapse. Restored princely states' rights via Queen's Proclamation. Lord Dalhousie (1848-56) was the GG BEFORE Canning. Lord Mayo (1869-72) — financial decentralisation, first census 1872, assassinated at Port Blair (only Viceroy killed in office). Lord Lytton (1876-80) — Vernacular Press Act 1878, Arms Act 1878, Royal Titles Act 1876 (Queen Victoria became 'Empress of India').

questions.stem: Which Viceroy is associated with the Partition of Bengal (1905), its reversal (1911), and the Delhi Darbar?

options.option_text: Lord Curzon ordered partition; Lord Hardinge II reversed it
Lord Minto ordered partition; Lord Curzon reversed it
Lord Lytton ordered partition; Lord Ripon reversed it
Lord Mayo ordered partition; Lord Elgin reversed it

questions.explanation: LORD CURZON (1899-1905) ordered the PARTITION OF BENGAL (October 1905), ostensibly for administrative convenience but actually to divide Hindu-majority West & Muslim-majority East — sparking the Swadeshi Movement. Also: founded ASI under John Marshall, Indian Universities Act 1904, Police Commission 1902, Railway Board 1905. LORD HARDINGE II (1910-16) — ANNULLED the Bengal partition at the DELHI DARBAR of 12 Dec 1911 (where King George V & Queen Mary were present; also shifted capital from Calcutta to Delhi). Survived a bomb attack 1912 by revolutionaries (Chandni Chowk bombing). Lord Minto II (1905-10) = Morley-Minto Reforms 1909 (separate electorates for Muslims, sowing seeds of two-nation theory).

questions.stem: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre (13 April 1919) took place during the tenure of which Viceroy?
questions.explanation: LORD CHELMSFORD (1916-21) was Viceroy during the Jallianwala Bagh massacre (Baisakhi day, 13 April 1919) at Amritsar — Brig-Gen Reginald Dyer ordered firing on unarmed crowd protesting the Rowlatt Act (passed March 1919). 379+ killed (official), ~1000+ (unofficial). Hunter Commission (1920) denounced Dyer. Tagore renounced his knighthood in protest. Chelmsford's tenure also saw: Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms 1919 (Dyarchy in provinces, Govt of India Act 1919), Rowlatt Act 1919, Non-Cooperation Movement launched Aug 1920. Lord Reading (1921-26) followed — Chauri Chaura 1922 and Non-Coop suspension. Lord Irwin (1926-31) — Simon Commission, Nehru Report, Dandi March, Gandhi-Irwin Pact 1931.

questions.stem: Lord Mountbatten was the last British Viceroy of India (March-August 1947). Who succeeded him as the FIRST (and only) Governor-General of INDEPENDENT India?
questions.explanation: Lord Louis Mountbatten (March 1947 — the LAST British Viceroy) continued as the FIRST Governor-General of INDEPENDENT India (15 Aug 1947 — 21 June 1948). He was succeeded by CHAKRAVARTI RAJAGOPALACHARI (C. Rajagopalachari, 'Rajaji') — the only INDIAN Governor-General of India (21 June 1948 — 26 Jan 1950). The office was ABOLISHED on 26 January 1950 when the Constitution came into force; Dr. Rajendra Prasad became the first PRESIDENT of India. In Pakistan: Mohammad Ali Jinnah was the first Governor-General (1947-48). Rajaji was also awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1954 — one of the first three recipients.

questions.stem: Which Viceroy introduced the 'Local Self-Government' principle through the Resolution of 1882, earning the title 'Father of Local Self-Government in India'?
questions.explanation: LORD RIPON (1880-84) is called the 'Father of Local Self-Government in India' for his Resolution of 18 May 1882 — expanding elected municipal and rural boards. Also: Hunter Commission 1882 (education — Indian Education Commission, the first on education policy), Ilbert Bill 1883 (allowing Indian judges to try Europeans — opposition led to its dilution and sparked political awakening), Factory Act 1881, repealed Vernacular Press Act. Lord Lytton (1876-80) preceded — the repressive predecessor (Delhi Durbar 1877 declaring Queen Victoria Empress of India, Arms Act 1878, Vernacular Press Act 1878, Afghan War 1878-80). Lord Dufferin (1884-88) followed — INC founded 1885 during his tenure. Lord Mayo (1869-72) — financial decentralisation, assassinated Port Blair.

questions.stem: The Indian Councils Act of 1892 and Gopal Krishna Gokhale's political emergence occurred during the tenure of which Viceroy?
questions.explanation: LORD LANSDOWNE (1888-94) was Viceroy during the Indian Councils Act 1892 (increased number of non-official members + limited indirect election — the seed of representative government). Also: creation of the Imperial Library (now National Library, Kolkata); Age of Consent Act 1891. LORD ELGIN II (1894-99) — the Plague of Bombay 1896, assassination of the Rand brothers by Chapekar Brothers (Pune 1897), famine 1896-97. LORD DUFFERIN (1884-88) — INC founded 1885 (A.O. Hume), 3rd Anglo-Burmese War 1885, annexation of Upper Burma. LORD CURZON (1899-1905) — later, as noted, partition of Bengal.
